=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:
  SPA-N-001: General liability cap
  SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
  SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
  SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
  SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
  SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope

  SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses

  SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
  SPA-N-014: Category separation
  SPA-N-015: Title verification
  SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms

# Project Kestrel – Buyer-side review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Overall read:** The Seller Update describes the package as "fair and balanced"; it is not. It is a Seller-favourable regime (single cap for everything, 18-month limit, knowledge sweeper, data-room general disclosure) layered over a Disclosure Letter that, read carefully, *contradicts* several of the Update's reassurances (Bluefen "addressed" but no consent; Riverlark "addressed" but undischarged; bonuses "a matter for the Seller" but missing from funds flow). Note also the data room cut-off is 22 September 2026 — six weeks stale as of today — so a bring-down disclosure and refreshed DD-010/DD-006 should be required before signing.

| # | Issue | Seller position | Buyer should want | Recommendation / reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001** | General liability cap | 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims (cl 12.1). | Higher cap – target 100% of price, settle no lower than 40–50% (AUD 9.6–12m); cap applies to *general* warranties only. | **Reject 20%; counter at 100%, fallback 50%.** Known exposures (Riverlark 3.2m, bonuses 0.42m, Ironquay 0.18m, Sandbar 0.33m, open privacy incident) already approach the cap before any unknown breach. |
| **SPA-N-002** | De minimis & basket | AUD 25k per claim; AUD 250k basket; *excess-only* recovery (deductible). | Lower de minimis (~AUD 10k, ~0.04% of price), basket ~AUD 120–240k (0.5–1%), **tipping** (first-dollar) basket; related claims aggregated; indemnity/fundamental/tax claims excluded from both. | **Accept thresholds in principle but convert to tipping basket, lower de minimis, add aggregation of series claims.** A 250k deductible plus 25k per-claim floor would wipe out most realistic mid-size claims (e.g. the three 110k Sandbar items individually). |
| **SPA-N-003** | General claims time limit | 18 months from Completion; plus a sweeper that "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise". | 24 months for general warranties (two audit cycles); 7 years for tax; indefinite / statutory limitation for title & capacity; delete the sweeper. | **Counter at 24 months; strike the sweeper entirely.** 18 months may expire before the first full post-Completion audited accounts are finalised, and the sweeper silently drags tax, title and indemnities into the 18-month window. |
| **SPA-N-004** | Fundamental/Title regime | Capacity and title warranties subject to the same cap and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity". | Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, solvency, share capital) capped at 100% of price and surviving for the full statutory limitation period (6 yrs NSW) or indefinitely. | **Reject outright.** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to accept recovering only 20% of price if the Buyer does not actually own the company; this is market-standard and non-negotiable. |
| **SPA-N-005** | Fraud carve-out | None expressed; cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 say limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" – which on its face would include fraud. | Express carve-out: no cap, threshold, time limit, knowledge qualifier, non-reliance or exclusive-remedy provision applies to fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation, wilful concealment or wilful default by the Seller or its officers. | **Insert express fraud/wilful misconduct carve-out from every limitation.** An attempt to limit liability for fraud is likely unenforceable anyway (and sits badly with ACL s 18), but silence invites a dispute and the "all Claims of any nature" wording is an overreach. |
| **SPA-N-006** | Disclosure scope | General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012 as at 22 Sep 2026), the Accounts, statutory registers and *all publicly searchable records* (DL 1.1–1.2), with a non-admission clause (1.4). | Only matters "fairly disclosed" – specifically, with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter – in a Disclosure Letter with cross-referenced data-room documents; no general disclosure of the whole data room or public registers; bring-down disclosure to signing/Completion with Buyer right to walk or price-adjust. | **Reject general disclosure; require "fair disclosure" standard and a bring-down.** Blanket disclosure of a data room plus public records converts every warranty into a nullity, and the DL itself (cl 11) admits it is incomplete and six weeks stale. |
| **SPA-N-007** | Buyer knowledge qualifier | No claim for any matter the Buyer *or its advisers* had knowledge of, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records" (cl 8.3). | Delete, or confine to actual knowledge of a short named list of Buyer deal-team individuals, derived solely from matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter; expressly exclude constructive/imputed knowledge, advisers' knowledge, and "discoverable" matters. | **Strike cl 8.3; fallback is actual knowledge of 2–3 named individuals.** "Discoverable from public records" is constructive knowledge of the world and, combined with SPA-N-006, would eliminate the warranty package. |
| **SPA-N-008** | Bluefen consent | Update says consent is "addressed", Seller to use "reasonable endeavours", condition deemed satisfied on delivery of written consent. DL 2 admits **no** final consent and **no** evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are met. | Bluefen consent (and satisfaction/waiver of the 11.3 conditions, in Buyer-approved form, unconditional and not subject to revised pricing) as a Condition Precedent for the Buyer's benefit only; Seller "best/all reasonable endeavours"; Buyer walk right; alternatively a specific revenue indemnity or price retention. | **Make it a CP with Buyer-approved form, waivable only by the Buyer.** ~30% of revenue (AUD 3.6m) turns on this contract and the Seller's own letter confirms it is not in hand – "addressed" is not the same as obtained. |
| **SPA-N-009** | Riverlark facility | ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided *following* Completion" (cl 2/7). DL 3 confirms no repayment and no discharge of security. | Debt-free/cash-free means repaid *at* Completion from the purchase price via a payout letter and deed of release/discharge of all security (PPSR discharge) delivered as a Completion deliverable; facility change-of-control (cl 8.1) consent or payout confirmed pre-Completion; price reduced by any amount not discharged. | **Reject post-Completion release; require payout letter, release and PPSR discharge at Completion with the debt deducted in the funds flow.** Otherwise the Buyer pays a debt-free price and acquires a company still carrying AUD 3.2m of secured debt with a triggered change-of-control default. |
| **SPA-N-010** | Employee bonuses | DD-005 closing bonuses (AUD 420k) are "a matter for the Seller" and "not separately itemised" in the funds flow. DL 5 confirms they are omitted and that on-costs (payroll tax, super) are unquantified. | Transaction bonuses plus all on-costs (super, payroll tax, leave accruals) treated as Transaction Costs / Debt-like items and deducted from the price in the funds flow or paid by the Seller at Completion; specific indemnity for any shortfall and for employee claims; confirm treatment of "continued-employment" conditions so the Buyer isn't funding retention the Seller promised. | **Itemise AUD 420k + on-costs (est. ~AUD 480–500k gross) in the funds flow as a price deduction, backed by a specific indemnity.** If they're genuinely "the Seller's matter", the Seller should have no objection to paying them; leaving them out means the Company (i.e. the Buyer) pays. |
| **SPA-N-011** | Ironquay IP indemnity | Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment (AUD 180k) and "considered adequate" (cl 11.1). DL 4: title to SOW3 Project Materials passes only on *cleared* payment; AUD 180k still open; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in data room. | Pre-Completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment **and** a confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay; failing that, a Completion retention; indemnity should cover the full consequences of defective title to the SOW3 deliverables (loss of use, re-development, third-party claims, infringement), not just the fee, and sit outside cap/basket/time limits. | **Require payment + confirmatory assignment as a Completion deliverable; widen indemnity to consequential IP loss, uncapped by cl 12.** The exposure is not AUD 180k, it is the value of the software/materials the Company does not yet own. |
| **SPA-N-012** | Export/privacy incident | "Preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material" (cl 4.6/Sch 6). DL 6: link sent to wrong external address, ~1,240 records with personal information, access/scope/notification unresolved as at 22 Sep. | Updated incident report and legal assessment (Privacy Act 1988 NDB scheme – has the "eligible data breach" assessment been completed within the 30-day window?); specific indemnity for all regulator action, notification costs, customer claims and remediation, outside cap/basket/time limit; warranty that no notifiable breach has occurred except as specifically disclosed; CP or Completion deliverable confirming assessment outcome. | **Treat as a known contingent liability: specific indemnity outside cl 12 plus pre-signing bring-down of the investigation.** The Seller's "not material" is an opinion the DL expressly refuses to make; the 30-day NDB assessment window from the incident has almost certainly lapsed and Bluefen/other customer data may be involved. |
| **SPA-N-013** | Sandbar renewals | Three renewals, AUD 110k each (AUD 330k total), described as "ordinary-course operating costs". DL 8: Seller does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. | Clarity on timing: if the renewals fall due pre-Completion or relate to pre-Completion periods, they are Seller costs/accrued liabilities for the completion accounts; confirm no single contract has been split to fall under the AUD 25k/110k thresholds; copies of all three with termination rights; pre-Completion covenant requiring Buyer consent to renew. | **Require the three contracts to be treated as one aggregated item in the completion accounts/working capital and add a conduct-of-business consent right.** Three identical AUD 110k items "read together" is a classic de minimis/basket avoidance pattern and the Seller declines to call them ordinary course in its own letter. |
| **SPA-N-014** | Category separation | Single regime: all limitations, caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.3/12.8/20.5). | Distinct categories with distinct limits: (i) general warranties – cap/basket/18–24 mths; (ii) fundamental/title/capacity – 100% price, 6 yrs+; (iii) tax – 100% price, 7 yrs; (iv) specific indemnities (Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay, privacy, Bluefen) – uncapped or capped at price, no basket, no knowledge qualifier; (v) fraud – no limits; (vi) Seller covenants (leakage, restraint) – no limits. | **Rewrite cl 12–13 as a tiered schedule and delete every "all Claims" sweeper.** A single regime is the mechanism that makes SPA-N-001, 003, 004, 005 and 011/012 bite; fixing them individually is pointless if the sweepers remain. |
| **SPA-N-015** | Title verification | Title "evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012"; DL 10 notes this is only the source relied on and the Buyer has not verified. | Buyer to run its own ASIC extract/company search and PPSR search immediately pre-signing and again pre-Completion; Seller to deliver executed transfers, share certificates (or indemnity for lost certificates), board minutes approving transfer and registration, evidence that no security interest, option or trust affects the shares; unlimited title warranty per SPA-N-004. | **Do our own ASIC and PPSR searches now and repeat at Completion; do not rely on DD-012.** A company-maintained register is only prima facie evidence; the Seller's own letter disclaims that the Buyer has verified anything. |
| **SPA-N-016** | Tax/IP open terms | "Settled under the general regime above" – i.e. 20% cap, 18-month limit, AUD 25k/250k thresholds, general disclosure. | Tax: tax indemnity (not just warranty) for all pre-Completion tax, 7-year limit, 100% cap, no basket, no knowledge qualifier, control of tax audits. IP: warranties that the Company owns or validly licenses all IP needed for the business, no infringement, all contractor/employee IP assigned (Ironquay is a live example), open-source compliance; 100% cap or at least a higher tier; survival 5–6 yrs. | **Not settled – reopen both and move them to the fundamental/indemnity tiers.** An analytics business's value *is* its IP and its tax history; ATO review periods alone (4 years, longer for fraud/evasion) outlast an 18-month limit. |

## Priority order for the mark-up

1. **Deal-breakers to fix before anything else:** SPA-N-014 (category separation – unlocks everything), SPA-N-009 (Riverlark discharge at Completion), SPA-N-008 (Bluefen as a true CP), SPA-N-004/005 (fundamental and fraud carve-outs).
2. **Price/funds-flow corrections (quantifiable now):** Riverlark AUD 3.2m, bonuses ~AUD 0.42m + on-costs, Ironquay AUD 0.18m, Sandbar AUD 0.33m where accrued → roughly **AUD 4.1–4.2m** that should come off the headline AUD 24m or be paid by the Seller at Completion, plus a retention/escrow for the privacy incident.
3. **Protection regime:** SPA-N-001/002/003 (cap, basket, time) and SPA-N-006/007 (disclosure and knowledge) – these are the standard negotiable terms, but only worth negotiating once items 1–2 are fixed.
4. **Information requests before signing:** bring-down of the data room from 22 Sep to a date within 5 business days of signing; Bluefen correspondence; Riverlark payout letter; Ironquay receipt/assignment; privacy incident assessment and NDB conclusion; all three Sandbar contracts; our own ASIC/PPSR searches.

Happy to turn this into a clause-by-clause mark-up of cl 2, 3, 6, 8, 9, 11, 12, 13 and 20, or a Buyer issues list for the next call with Harbourglass counsel.
